why: N32. The photograph reader, trialled as an open replacement for the agent session that currently fills the criteria sheet (`notes/JOYCAPTION.md`). JoyCaption Beta One is Llama 3.1 8B + a SigLIP2 vision tower on the LLaVA architecture, and it is the only surveyed candidate that ships a Danbooru tag mode AND is trained on photographs -- the property WD14 lacks, which is why WD14 scores 0.47 on photographs against 0.73 on renders (F29). Hosted locally through Ollama, so the client is stdlib `urllib` against a localhost port and no Python dependency is added.
not_in_eval_models_json: A prototype artifact, recorded the way round 1 recorded Qwen and the raena LoRA and the way `wd14_models.json` records the evaluator: beside the prototype, never in the tracked eval manifest, whose byte-identical derivation this branch must not disturb. Its licence is therefore recorded HERE and not in `scripts/eval_licences.md`, which belongs to `eval_models.json`.
why_this_repository: Because it is the only requantisation that ships the vision projector. Checked 2026-09-11 and re-checked 2026-09-12: `mradermacher/llama-joycaption-beta-one-hf-llava-GGUF` and `Mungert/llama-joycaption-beta-one-hf-llava-GGUF` contain NO mmproj at all. A LLaVA-family model without its projector loads, answers fluently and CANNOT SEE THE IMAGE -- the failure is silent, which is why N33's sight gate has to be falsifiable rather than a single `describe this` prompt. List a repository's contents before downloading it, not after.
urls_pin_the_revision: Unlike `wd14_models.json`, whose sources resolve through `main`. A digest check catches a repository that moved; a pinned revision stops it moving. Both are here: the revision above is in every source URL, and the digest is still verified on every run.

licence.summary: NOT cleanly Apache-2.0, and both `notes/READER.md` and `notes/JOYCAPTION.md` say that it is. Recorded deviation, in the shape `scripts/eval_licences.md` uses for glintr100.

layers.note: SPDX `Apache-2.0`, confirmed through the GitHub licence API. This is the claim both notes are quoting, and it covers the repository's CODE.
The model card carries NO `license` field. Its README says "Free and Open: Released for free, open weights, no restrictions" -- prose, not an SPDX identifier and not a licence text.

**This is the deviation.** The Llama 3.1 Community License is not Apache-2.0: it carries naming, acceptable-use and 700M-MAU terms, and the base repository is gated (`gated: manual`). A fine-tune of it is a derivative. The upstream author's "no restrictions" cannot grant more than he received.

No `license` field and the README states no terms of its own -- it says only that the quants were made for KoboldCpp 1.91+. `concedo` is the KoboldCpp author. The gap is recorded rather than assumed away.

licence.reading: Fine for this prototype, which renders locally, distributes no weights and links no code. It is NOT a settled position for anything that ships: a reader adopted into a version needs the Llama 3.1 terms read properly first, and that read is a task, not a footnote. Written down here so the trial is not later quoted as having cleared it.

entries_note: 5.80 GB for the pair, on a machine with 16 GiB of RAM and 43 GiB free (measured 2026-09-12). The mmproj is loaded ALONGSIDE the quant, never instead of it; the source repository's own README misnames the projector as `Llama-Joycaption-Beta-One-Hf-Llava-F16.gguf`, which is the 16 GB full-precision TEXT model. Pairing by that instruction gives a 21 GB download and no vision.

not_fetched.why: `JOYCAPTION.md` §7's quantisation check, and only that. The one data point we have is 0.688 from the public demo, which is presumably full precision; if the local Q4_K numbers come in far under it, quantisation is the FIRST suspect and this is the file that tests it. 9.42 GB fits the disk and is tight against 16 GiB of RAM, so it is not tried first. Its digest is recorded now so nobody has to re-derive it under the pressure of a bad result.
The full-precision text model. Recorded ONLY so it is never confused with the projector again -- see `entries_note`. 16 GB does not fit this machine's RAM and is out of scope.
